title: hotfix(slo-enforcer): tighten thresholds and stabilize regional failover ordering
author: Aditi Kumar
description: Motivation: We observed an incident where the SLO enforcer's regional failover ordering + backoff smoothing could trigger aggressive load-shedding in the secondary region during a transient network partition. This PR tightens threshold math, fixes ordering race conditions in the failover decision path, and adjusts the smoothing/backoff parameters to avoid thrashing. Summary of changes: - Fix race in regional failover ordering by ensuring deterministic evaluation order and adding a simple sequence token to failover events. - Tighten SLOEnforcer thresholds: only trigger inter-region failover when both 1) local failure rate > 5% AND 2) regional latency P95 > 2x baseline for 30s. Previously the second condition used a noisy rolling window which allowed short spikes to cause failovers. - Smooth backoff and load-shedding ramp: introduce an exponential smoothing factor and minimum stabilization window (15s) before shedding more than 10% traffic to a fallback. - Backfill unit & integration tests for ordering and threshold behavior; add a focused canary e2e that simulates a partial partition. - Minor docs and helm values to make the thresholds configurable by ops. Rollout plan: patch deployed as hotfix to Dedicated and Hosted control plane with a 50% canary for 30 minutes, then full rollout if no regression. Linked Linear tickets and incident notes included. Checklist: [x] reproduce locally with test harness [x] unit tests added [x] integration test added [x] canary config and helm values updated [x] docs/upgrade notes updated [x] post-deploy monitoring dashboard alert thresholds updated Backport: This is a production hotfix; main branch only. If requested we can backport to release/2026-02. Notes: The threshold tightening is intentionally conservative to avoid false positives. If customers observe higher error budgets, ops can adjust via the helm values (values.sloEnforcer.thresholds). For more context see Linear ENG-2145 and the incident postmortem (internal link).
